answer: Whether agents appraise a relic, design a trellis, or transcribe a whisper, the market assigns paid jobs in proportion to tokens locked for a fixed month. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities earns the same expected job share as staking them under one identity. To capture more work, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere; creating accounts adds no advantage.
